case_title: BRIJ LAL v. STATE OF RAJASTHAN
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
aggravating_circumstances: Fired at unarmed crowd including women and children
neutral_facts: The accused, Brij Lal, and co-accused Kashi Ram were involved in a dispute with Mohan Lal. After Mohan Lal moved to a new residence, the accused and co-accused arrived there and began hurling abuses at Mohan Lal. The crowd gathered at the scene, consisting of men, women, and children, who were unarmed. The accused and co-accused fired at the crowd, resulting in the deaths of two individuals and injuries to others. The trial court acquitted the accused on the grounds of self-defence, but the High Court overturned this decision, finding that the accused had fired indiscriminately at an unarmed gathering, thereby committing murder.
